_comment: Lazarus7 (c) 2026 lance6x5, MIT. Single source for the Diagnose wizard: read by src/Lazarus7.Triage.psm1 and docs/index.html. Steps starting with two spaces continue the previous step. Keep ASCII.

platforms.label: HP Stream 7 - came with Windows 8.1
platforms.hint: label TSW 7H - what Lazarus7 is built for

Windows.label: HP logo, then a blank black screen
HP logo keeps coming back (boot loop)
Automatic Repair loop / "Your PC ran into a problem"
Error 0xc0000225 "Your PC needs to be repaired" (also from F11)
Asks for a password BEFORE the HP logo (BIOS)
Windows 8.1 works - I want to back up / move to a new OS

Android.label: Boot logo, then black screen / boot loop
Asks for a password before the logo
Black screen, but the PC sees it over USB

unknown.title: Identify the tablet first
steps: Back label "TSW 7H", Windows logo, shipped with Windows 8.1 = HP Stream 7.
Android tablets: plug into a PC and run "Identify a tablet over USB".

dead.title: Revive the battery
steps: Charge with a 2 A wall charger + short cable for 4+ hours (not a PC port).
Hold Power 15-30 s (hard reset), release, then hold Power 5 s.
Try a second charger and cable before giving up.
Never any battery icon = dead battery or board; a battery swap is the fix.

password.title: BIOS / power-on password
steps: Enter a wrong password 3 times to get a halt code.
HP Support can turn the halt code + serial number into an unlock code.
There is no safe software bypass for this.

bitlocker.title: BitLocker recovery screen
steps: Windows 8.1 with Bing turns on Device Encryption when you sign in with a Microsoft account.
Get the key at https://account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey
No key? Data is unrecoverable, but F11 > Reset your PC or a recovery USB still works.

black.title: HP logo, then a blank black screen
steps: Charge 2+ hours, power on, then WAIT 15 minutes - updates or Automatic Repair can run behind a black screen.
USB keyboard on the OTG adapter: press Ctrl+Alt+Del, then Win+Ctrl+Shift+B (restarts the graphics driver).
Something appears = Windows is alive and the display driver is the problem.
Shine a flashlight at the screen: a faint image means the backlight failed (hardware).
Vol- + Power: if the startup menu shows, firmware and screen are fine. F2 -> storage (eMMC) test.
F11 -> Troubleshoot -> Advanced options: Startup Repair, then Startup Settings ->
"Enable low-resolution video" or Safe Mode. Last resort: Refresh your PC.
F11 also black or "partition missing" = WIMBoot recovery partition damaged: boot from USB
(recovery media, or a Debian stick - a picture in Debian proves the hardware is fine).

c0000225.title: 0xc0000225 - a required device can't be accessed
steps: The boot manager can't reach the boot files: a failing eMMC, a damaged/deleted WIMBoot
recovery partition, or a corrupted boot configuration (BCD) - the last one is fixable.
Vol- + Power -> F2 -> storage test FIRST. If the eMMC fails, stop: software can't fix it.
Storage OK: build a Windows 10 x86 stick (Microsoft ISO) with Lazarus7 - it includes the repair helper.
Boot it (F9, USB keyboard) -> Repair your computer -> Troubleshoot -> Startup Repair.
Still failing: Command Prompt -> D:\lazarus7\windows\Stream7-Repair.cmd (try E:/F: if D: is wrong).
It shows which partitions survived, checks WIMBoot + boot files, and can rebuild them (bcdboot).
WIMBoot partition gone = Windows 8.1 can't return without recovery media: install Windows 10 or Debian.

repair.title: Automatic Repair loop / "Your PC ran into a problem"
steps: Vol- + Power -> F2: run the storage (eMMC) test first - loops are often a failing eMMC.
Vol- + Power -> F11 -> Troubleshoot -> "Refresh your PC" (keeps your files).
Still broken: same menu -> "Reset your PC" (erases everything, back to factory 8.1).
Refresh/Reset fail = recovery partition damaged: restore from HP recovery media.

winpass.title: Forgot the Windows sign-in
steps: Microsoft account: reset it at https://account.live.com/password/reset, then
connect the tablet to Wi-Fi from the sign-in screen and use the new password.
Local account without a reset disk: no safe bypass.
Vol- + Power -> F11 -> "Reset your PC" restores factory Windows 8.1 (erases data).

logo.title: HP logo boot loop
steps: Vol- + Power -> F2: run the storage (eMMC) test first.
Vol- + Power -> F11: Refresh / Reset your PC, if the recovery partition survived.
Otherwise restore from an HP recovery USB, or deploy Linux.

noboot.title: "No bootable device"
steps: Windows is gone (often the WIMBoot recovery partition was deleted) or the UEFI lost its boot entry.
Restore Windows 8.1 from HP recovery media, or deploy Linux.
Had Linux already? Re-running the Lazarus7 post-install script fixes the boot entry.

boots.title: It boots Windows 8.1 - back it up before anything else
steps: Windows 8.1 is out of support (Jan 2023): OK offline, risky on the internet.
Make a Lazarus7 tablet toolkit USB and run lazarus7\windows\Stream7-Check.cmd on the tablet:
it saves serial, product number, firmware key, WIMBoot and BitLocker status.
From the same helper, make a recovery drive on a SECOND 8 GB+ stick. This tablet uses
WIMBoot, so the recovery partition IS your Windows - that stick is your way back.
Then turn off Fast Startup (helper option 1) and deploy Linux.

logo.title: Android boot loop
steps: Try stock recovery: Power + Vol+ (on the 2800 sometimes Vol+ AND Vol-).
Wipe data/factory reset, or "apply update from ADB" with an HP OTA zip.
No recovery? Rockchip loader mode + RKDevTool full flash.

noboot.title: Black screen but USB responds
steps: Plug into a PC and run "Identify a tablet over USB".
Rockchip VID 2207 = loader mode: full firmware flash is possible.

boots.title: It boots Android
steps: Enable USB debugging, then use ADB tools to reboot to recovery/bootloader.

fallback.title: No specific recommendation
steps: See docs/GUIDE.md.
